en.title: Ferriq Capsule
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia.
en.usage: Adults take 1 capsule at a time, once a day. Follow the prescribed dosage.
en.caution: Warning: an overdose in children aged 6 or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep out of the reach of children. Do not take this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, are an infant under 12 months, have hemochromatosis (a disorder in which iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism), hemosiderosis, non-iron-deficiency anemia, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Consult a pharmacist before use if you have a gastrointestinal disorder such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis, cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, low blood protein, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or are folate-deficient; if there is no improvement after about a month of use, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist. Follow the prescribed dosage and amount. Do not take with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, or antacids; consult a pharmacist when taking with antialdosterone agents or triamterene; avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea and milk or dairy during, before and after use. Stop taking it and consult a pharmacist if you develop erythema (red spots), skin disorders, itching, general malaise, breathing difficulty, hives, photosensitivity, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, coma, nausea, loss of appetite, weight loss, swelling, constipation, black stools, or stomach discomfort.
